hero.subtext: I spend most of my career translating between roadmaps and codebases — 7+ years leading product, and 4 years writing the code myself. That history means I still open the repo before I open the backlog: diagnosing issues directly in the source, reviewing pull requests, and shipping AI-assisted prototypes in days, not sprints.

case_studies.title: Product Strategy
case_studies.summary: The founder was attached to all four products. The MRR data said focus on one.
problem: Founder was running four separate product lines simultaneously, spreading dev and attention thin
No data-backed view of which product actually drove revenue
Founder resistant to narrowing focus, emotionally invested across all four
solution: Ran an MRR analysis across all four products to surface the actual revenue driver
Built the business case and presented it directly to challenge the founder's resistance to data-driven prioritization
Persuaded the founder to consolidate focus down to the single strongest product

impact.label: focus — realigned growth strategy and resourcing around the single highest-revenue product

case_studies.title: Better Product Culture
case_studies.summary: Feedback was unstructured and dev time was being spent on features nobody asked for.
problem: No structured intake for customer feedback, signal and noise mixed together
Dev cycles were being spent building features nobody asked for
solution: Introduced a structured process to collect and prioritize feedback
Separated actionable signal from noise before anything reached the dev queue

impact.label: cut in dev time spent on the wrong features

case_studies.title: Research on Customers
case_studies.summary: Standard NPS got low response rates. Built something simpler that customers would actually answer.
problem: No structured feedback system in place
Standard NPS was attempted first but ruled out — response rates were too low to be usable
solution: Designed a lightweight 1–5 CSAT process, captured via Customer Care immediately after ticket resolution
Supplemented with random check-in calls to catch customers who wouldn't otherwise respond

impact.label: average satisfaction score, reached within 2 months

case_studies.title: UX Redesign & Product-Led Growth
case_studies.summary: Freemium wasn't viable for IoT hardware. Built a self-serve product experience anyway.
problem: IoT-based GPS-tracking product couldn't offer freemium or free trial (hardware/service cost structure makes it economically unviable)
No self-serve path, meant every prospect needed a manual sales touch before seeing the product
solution: Redesigned the onboarding flow and added a registration page allowing any visitor to self-register, capturing their info as a lead

Built auto-login with demo credentials so visitors could experience the live product immediately — since a freshly registered account has no real GPS device attached yet, demo access was the only way to show the product before purchase

case_studies.title: Improved Architecture to Migrate Clients
case_studies.summary: Migrated live, paying clients off a white-labeled platform onto a self-hosted system, near-zero downtime.
problem: Needed to migrate live, paying GPS-tracking clients off a white-labeled third-party platform onto a self-hosted system

Migration had to happen with near-zero service disruption to active users — the target was absolute zero, achieved in staging; production carried additional hardware variables outside this story's scope
Needed enforceable, configurable concurrent-session limits as part of the new auth layer
solution: Engineered a dual-backend authentication layer enabling clients to run across both old and new systems during transition
Built custom middleware to enforce configurable concurrent-session limits

impact.label: service disruption during live client migration
of mobile phone numbers updated in CRM & client DB as a side-effect of the migration

case_studies.title: Successful Product Launch
case_studies.summary: Coordinating six tech stacks for a launch, without a Tech Lead in the room.
problem: Upgraded product launch required coordinating six distinct tech stacks simultaneously
Needed direct engineering-level coordination, not just spec handoff, across mobile, web, backend, and IoT teams
solution: Led the cross-functional team in absence of a Tech Lead, working directly with engineers across Android (Kotlin), iOS (Swift), React, Django, Laravel, and Node.js (IoT device parser)
Coordinated launch sequencing across all platforms concurrently

impact.label: ahead of deadline — Android app launch

case_studies.industry: SaaS, GPS-tracking platform — Web, Android & iOS apps, IoT

case_studies.title: Technical Project Management
case_studies.summary: Poor task granularity and missed dependencies were costing delivery time. Fixed it with structure.
problem: Project delivery suffered from poor task granularity, overlapping responsibilities, and missed dependencies
Needed tighter control across scope, time, and budget simultaneously
solution: Built a granular Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) to control scope, time, and budget
Synced task hierarchy with the Agile backlog for clarity
case_studies.industry: SaaS, GPS-tracking platform, Android & iOS apps

case_studies.title: Service Launch
case_studies.summary: COVID created urgent demand for a life-saving service. Launched it fast, remotely, on budget.
problem: COVID-19 created urgent demand for an oxygen supply service for patients, under pressure to launch fast
Operating remotely with cost pressure on a time-sensitive humanitarian & medical service
solution: Designed the online (Facebook-based) launch program for the oxygen supply service end-to-end

impact.label: kept a life-saving oxygen service within budget during a crisis

case_studies.industry: Healthcare/medical supply, remote service launch (during lockdown)

case_studies.title: Founding PM
case_studies.summary: Joined as a co-founder for minimal remuneration, so the tech founder didn't have to hire.
problem: Early-stage startup, co-founded from scratch, no existing product, process, or operational structure to inherit
Needed to control burn rate as a founding-stage priority while still building a product/project management function
solution: Joined as a co-founder for minimal remuneration alongside the tech founder, who needed an additional person but couldn't yet justify hiring a salaried employee
Owned product and project management as part of a small founding team

impact.label: reduction in operational cost — by structuring the arrangement as a co-founder stake instead of a hire

services.title: Fractional / Technical Product Manager
services.description: Embedded PM support for teams that need product judgment and technical fluency in the same person — roadmap ownership, backlog discipline, and the ability to review a PR or debug a production issue when needed.

services.title: Product Strategy Advisory
services.description: Outside-in review of where a product or product line actually stands — MRR-driven prioritization, scope discipline, and the kind of data-backed case that can shift a founder's mind on focus.

services.title: AI-Native MVP Build
services.description: Rapid, AI-assisted prototyping from spec to a working MVP — 15 to 30 day delivery, using tools like Loveable and Replit alongside traditional architecture and code review.

services.title: Team Training & Workshops
services.description: Hands-on training for product and engineering teams — Agile/Scrum fundamentals, Java/Spring Boot, or structuring a WBS that actually holds up under delivery pressure.

footer.cta: Open to technical PM roles, founding-team opportunities, and product advisory work — especially where someone needs to move between strategy and the codebase without a translator.
